newsitem.title: USA: Salton/Maxim sees benefit from pacts.
newsitem.headline: Salton/Maxim sees benefit from pacts.

text.p: Salton/Maxim Housewares Inc said Tuesday it expects its previously announced sales agreements with Kmart Corp and Winmere-Durable Holdings to boost sales and profits.

"We are very pleased with Salton/Maxim's rapid sales growth," Leonhard Dreimann, chief executive officer, said in a statement. "The distribution agreement we signed with Kmart is clearly having the desired impact on our top-line results. We believe both the Kmart and Windmere...agreements have positioned us for accelerated long-term growth in both sales and profitability."

Earlier, Salton/Maxim reported a net loss for the third quarter ended March 29 of $0.05 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.11 a share. Sales for the quarter rose 106 percent to $41.7 million from $20.2 million.

The company said the net loss was attributed to increased advertising expense, start-up costs associated with its supply agreement with Kmart, and start-up costs related to the launch of the Farberware product line.

Salton/Maxim previously agreed to supply Kmart with a range of small electrical appliances, personal care products and other products under the White-Westinghouse brand. It also signed an exclusive worldwide distribution agreement with Windmere to market electric products under the Farberware brand name.
